What was the most valuable thing about D: I like the conversational aspect of it. I don't like building plans on other AI platforms because as soon as they are built, they are static. I like how you could modify this one based on how you're feeling, and it will then update the whole plan. For instance, if I am traveling, I could say a run won't work and it will reschedule it.
What would you change about Daybreak?: There was about a week or so where it kept asking me what trail I wanted to run for a certain run that was on my schedule. I kept ignoring it, and it kept asking me. However, I finally asked that it not ask me specific trails as I normally wing it, and it modified itself. So really no complaint! - I liked how it was responsive to the way I wanted it to be.
Any other thoughts? (optional): I'm sorry it has to be put on hold. I liked it. I think I would need another month or so to have it fully understand my routine and see if it improves my training. You crushed this one Dave!!! Bring it back!!!

What was the most valuable thing about D: I like the interface of being able to "chat" through the goals. Simply put, it's easier to chat through specific goals and issues than to input them as set in stone.
What would you change about Daybreak?: I wondered to some degree how much it was actually helpful vs just a little addictive to chat with someone about my goals. Like, the actual plans it made for me always seemed slightly off or overly complicated — not sure why. So I kinda ignored the daily schedule it gave me, since most of the time it was a slight miss for me. Instead, I found it useful to be like, "OK, this week, I'm hoping to do this. Does that feel like the right amount? What should I do if my hamstring is acting up? I had to change plans, should I do 7 miles today given what I've done this week?"
Any other thoughts? (optional): I was using Claude before Daybreak for the same reasons, just without the Strava connection. I wasn't entirely sure why to keep using Daybreak instead of Claude.

What was the most valuable thing about D: The daily interactions are nice. I already use LLMs extensively for fitness planning and analysis but the context is frequently split across multiple threads and i have to keep pulling in the relevant data about what I want to accomplish and what I am trying to optimize for. Having this work passively is quite nice and pushes me to be more balanced in my training.
What would you change about Daybreak?: I hate using Telegram. Easy to integrate with but have to pay to block obvious spam. A separate app would be nice is many ways.
Any other thoughts? (optional): I've been thinking for a while that it would be fun to create a way to free your data from Strava so that others could build integrations on it. Either making it an intermediate platform that you upload to and then it uploads to Strava or that is pulls data from Stava and gives you an API to leverage with other platforms.

What was the most valuable thing about D: It’s adaptibility when I kept changing my plans and goals. Also maybe it Sens minor but I rally liked the calendar syncing!
What would you change about Daybreak?: I loved all of it! Maybe my only negative was when it started doing the chat thing a couple days ago? Like “where are you going on vacation” when I said I needed to change my schedule
Any other thoughts? (optional): I don’t know anything about how to make an app but the whole experience seemed very elegant and smooth and I wish it still existed!
